title: Why So Many Teachers Struggle With Classroom Management https://smartclassroommanagement.com/2021/04/03/teachers-struggle-with-classroom-management/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin argues that the gap between excellent and average classrooms is far larger than most teachers realize, and traces it to what he calls 'the great disconnect' — teachers who have never witnessed genuine whole-class transformation simply can't believe it's achievable, so they default to blaming their roster instead. He attributes the wider problem to teacher-training programs that underemphasize classroom management or teach ineffective tactics like rewards and false praise, leaving new teachers unprepared and eventually demoralized. His central claim is that classroom management is a learnable, specific skill rather than an innate gift, and that once a teacher directly experiences what's possible, disbelief becomes impossible to sustain, urging skeptical readers to test the SCM approach for one month as proof.

quotes: Allow me to let you in on a secret: There is a shocking difference between classrooms run by teachers with excellent classroom management and everyone else.
The result is that teachers enter the profession unprepared. They lose confidence and quit or spend the rest of their career pretending to be a good teacher.
The deeper reason that there is such a profound difference between good teachers and the rest, however, is what I call the great disconnect.
If you don’t know what’s possible, if you’ve never seen whole-class transformation, then it’s hard to believe it exists.
It isn’t quantum physics. There are skills you can learn that will allow you to walk into any classroom in the world and transform those students into your dream class .
If you don’t believe me, give us a chance to prove it to you. Put SCM to the test for one month.
